title: Irrational square root: a square diagonal

purpose: Why can the exact diagonal-to-side ratio have no whole-number fraction?
meaning: The ratio of a square’s diagonal to its side is the positive square root of two. It is irrational: no ratio of integers equals it. Consecutive finite continued-fraction convergents give useful rational approximations without making the ratio itself rational.

properties.claim: The ratio of a square’s diagonal to its side is the positive square root of two. It is irrational: no ratio of integers equals it. Consecutive finite continued-fraction convergents give useful rational approximations without making the ratio itself rational.
properties.conditions: The square side is 0.5 to 3 metres. The eight choices are consecutive continued-fraction convergents 1/1 through 577/408. Each is rational; no finite decimal or finite picture proves irrationality. The parity argument in the card proves that √2 is not a ratio of integers. Drawing directions use equal metre scales.
properties.derivation: For a unit square, Pythagoras gives d²=1²+1²=2, hence d=√2. Suppose √2=p/q for coprime positive integers p and q. Then p²=2q², so p² is even, hence p is even. Write p=2t. Substitution gives q²=2t², so q is also even, contradicting coprimality. Thus no integer ratio equals √2. Scaling both legs to s gives diagonal s√2. The finite convergents displayed here approximate this length; the parity contradiction, rather than their decimal agreement, proves irrationality.
